'''Laurent Clozel''' (born 23 October 1953 in [[Gap, Hautes-Alpes|Gap]], France) is a French [[mathematician]] and professor at [[Paris-Saclay University]]. His mathematical work is in the area of [[automorphic form]]s, including the [[Langlands program]].

== Career and distinctions ==

Clozel was a student at the [[École normale supérieure]] and later obtained a Ph.D. under [[Michel Duflo]] and [[Paul Gérardin]].<ref>[http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=56565 Mathematics Genealogy Project]</ref>

He received the [[Elie Cartan Prize|Prix Élie Cartan]] of the French Academy for his work on [[Base change lifting|base change]] for automorphic forms. He was an invited speaker at the 1986 [[International congress of mathematicians]] in [[Berkeley, California|Berkeley]], talking about "Base change for GL(''n'')".

Together with [[Richard Taylor (mathematician)|Richard Taylor]], [[Nicholas Shepherd-Barron]], and [[Michael Harris (mathematician)|Michael Harris]] he proved the [[Sato–Tate conjecture]].<ref>{{Citation| last1=Clozel| first1=Laurent| last2=Harris| first2=Michael| last3=Taylor| first3=Richard| title=Automorphy for some ''ℓ''-adic lifts of automorphic mod&nbsp;''ℓ'' Galois representations| journal=Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci.| volume=108| year=2008| pages=1&ndash;181| doi=10.1007/s10240-008-0016-1| mr=2470687| citeseerx=10.1.1.143.9755| s2cid=189785507}}</ref>
